header: Dallas just flipped the temperature of fall camp.
body:
Fall camp stopped being a depth-chart exercise the second Dallas Wilson started winning the grass.

Not a practice-report compliment. The ball is coming out cleaner, the releases are getting dirtier for DBs, and the offense suddenly has a true perimeter problem to build around. Camp noise compresses into one question: who can keep up with him.

Dijon Johnson is the other half. Sumrall already put a 22.5 on him before camp opened — not a Practice GPS flex, a staff note that the athlete matches the tape. Next to Dallas, Florida does not need two deep threats who look the same. One stresses the sideline. One punishes leverage after the catch.

Vault read from week one: Dallas is the temperature, Dijon is the accelerant, and everyone else either rises to that speed or watches it leave them.

Stay ahead of the board on FutureCast.
notes: Dijon 22.5 is pre-camp Sumrall note — not Practice GPS.
Vault voice, not beat-notebook laundry list.
